Toolbox/JSON Unescape & Escape — Quotes, Unicode and Newlines
Runs locally
ENCODING

JSON unescape & escape

Read escaped JSON strings or turn plain text into a JSON string. Handle quotes, backslashes, newlines and Unicode one layer at a time, in your browser.

One layer per conversion

Choose whether your input includes its outer quotes. Up to 1 million UTF-16 code units. Input is treated as text.

Unescaping one string does not execute its contents or format a whole JSON document.

A LITTLE CONTEXT

How to unescape a JSON string

Select Complete JSON string when the input includes outer double quotes. Select Escaped string content when you have only the contents between those quotes. The result is plain text; braces in that text do not change its type.

Escaped JSON string → one decoded text layer

References: MDN: JSON.parse and JSON grammar · MDN: JSON.stringify

Good to know

How do I escape double quotes in JSON?

Use Escape mode with your original plain text. A quote becomes \" inside the encoded string, and a backslash becomes \\. Leave Include outer double quotes selected when the destination expects a complete JSON string.

Why are backslashes still visible?

The original value may contain more than one layer of string encoding, or its actual text may contain backslashes. Each conversion removes one layer. The extra button appears only when the result is itself a complete JSON string.

Does this format an entire JSON object?

No. Unescape expects a JSON string or escaped string contents. Objects, arrays, numbers, booleans and null are different JSON values and are rejected in Complete JSON string mode.

Can I convert an empty string?

Yes. In Unescape mode, use the complete input "" or the Empty string example. In Escape mode, clear the input and select Escape text to produce "". An empty decoded result can be downloaded as a zero-byte text file.

Why is a Unicode escape rejected?

Malformed escape sequences are rejected. This tool also requires well-formed Unicode text, so a decoded unpaired UTF-16 surrogate is rejected even though JSON parsers can represent such a code unit.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

Quotes, newlines and nested strings

Use a complete example and choose its input format deliberately.

InputInput formatResult
"Hello\nworld"Complete JSON stringTwo lines of text
Hello\nworldEscaped string contentThe same two lines
"\u4e2d\u6587"Complete JSON string中文
{"ok":true}Complete JSON stringRejected: this is an object, not a string

Escaping turns text into a representation that can fit inside a JSON string. It does not encrypt it. This is a different operation from URL decoding, HTML entity decoding or Base64 decoding. For alphabet and byte issues, see the Base64 troubleshooting guide. Inputs are held in memory and are not put into URLs or sent to a conversion service.
